title: Verb + -ing or to … 3 (like / would like etc.)

exercises.instruction: Write sentences about yourself. Do you like these activities? Choose from these verbs: like / don’t like, love, hate, enjoy, don’t mind
modelAnswers: I don’t like to be alone.

items.prompt: (flying)
(playing cards)
(being alone)
modelAnswers: I don’t like to be alone.

items.prompt: (going to museums)
(cooking)
(getting up early)

exercises.instruction: Make sentences using -ing or to … . Sometimes either form is possible.

items.prompt: Paul lives in Berlin now. It’s nice. He likes it. (He / like / live / there)
Jane is a biology teacher. She likes her job. (She / like / teach / biology)
Joe always has his camera with him and takes a lot of pictures. (He / like / take / pictures)
I used to work in a supermarket. I didn’t like it much. (I / not / like / work / there)
Rachel is studying medicine. She likes it. (She / like / study / medicine)
Dan is famous, but he doesn’t like it. (He / not / like / be / famous)
Jennifer is a very careful person. She doesn’t take many risks. (She / not / like / take / risks)
answers: She doesn’t like to take risks.

items.prompt: I don’t like surprises. (I / like / know / things / in advance)
answers: I like to know things in advance.

exercises.instruction: Write sentences using would … to have (done). Use the verbs in brackets.

items.prompt: It’s a shame I couldn’t go to the party. (like)
answers: I would like to have gone to the party.

items.prompt: It’s a shame I didn’t see the programme. (like)
answers: I would like to have seen the programme.
I’d like to have seen the programme.

items.prompt: I’m glad I didn’t lose my watch. (hate)
answers: I would hate to have lost my watch.
I’d hate to have lost my watch.

items.prompt: It’s too bad I didn’t meet your parents. (love)
answers: I would love to have met your parents.
I’d love to have met your parents.

items.prompt: I’m glad I wasn’t alone. (not / like)
answers: I wouldn’t like to have been alone.

items.prompt: We should have travelled by train. (prefer)
answers: I would prefer to have travelled by train.
I’d prefer to have travelled by train.
